title: Induced componentwise maps on inverse limits
statement: Given three towers of R-modules and componentwise linear maps α and β commuting with successor transition maps, there are R-linear maps on the inverse limits whose coordinate projections are α and β applied coordinatewise.

proof.text: For any family in the target tower compatible with successor transitions, use Mathlib CategoryTheory.NatTrans.ofOpSequence from the constant PUnit functor to the underlying-type tower. Naturality on all arrows proves that the family is a section. This is the proved private helper tower_family_compatible.

For x in limit F, apply alpha to all its projections. The successor compatibility follows from h_alpha and limit.w. Transfer this section back to an element of limit G using Types.isLimitEquivSections for the limit cone preserved by ModuleCat.forget. Types.isLimitEquivSections_symm_apply gives every projection equation.

Prove additivity and scalar compatibility by Concrete.limit_ext: each projection of the constructed map agrees with alpha composed with the corresponding projection, and both maps are linear. This completes the proved private helper tower_induced_map. Apply it to alpha and beta and assemble the two maps and their projection equations.

proof_origin.place: NatTrans.ofOpSequence; Types.isLimitEquivSections and isLimitEquivSections_symm_apply; Concrete.limit_ext; componentwise construction of Stacks Algebra Lemma 03CA

lean.statement: theorem tower_limit_induced_maps (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R) (H : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{t} R) (α : ∀ n : ℕ, F.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] G.obj (Opposite.op n)) (β : ∀ n : ℕ, G.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] H.obj (Opposite.op n)) (hα : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : F.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (α (n + 1) x) = α n (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) (hβ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : G.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), H.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (β (n + 1) x) = β n (G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) : ∃ (U : ↑(limit F) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit G)) (V : ↑(limit G) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit H)), (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit F)), limit.π G (Opposite.op n) (U x) = α n (limit.π F (Opposite.op n) x)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit G)), limit.π H (Opposite.op n) (V x) = β n (limit.π G (Opposite.op n) x))
